chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said, 'How many are permissible from Mut'ah?' He said, then he said: 'They are at the status of the slave girls.'
ai.seo_question: What is the limit on the number of wives in Shia temporary marriage (Mut'ah)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the number of temporary wives (Mut'ah) is not restricted to four, equating their status to that of slave girls. This comparison highlights that just as a man could possess multiple slave women, he could contract Mut'ah with multiple women simultaneously, a key distinction from the permanent marriage limit. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Mut'ah in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the strict monogamy or polygyny limits of permanent marriage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I said, ‘How many (wives) are Permissible from the Mut’a?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are at the status of the slave girls (no limit)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about how many are lawful for al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage).
He (the Imam) said, ‘Their case is similar to slave-girls.’”
